title: An owner who borrows to fund current payouts turns borrowed money into debt the business cannot service without growth
body:
- An owner who uses borrowed money to fund payouts to themselves instead of expanding productive capacity extracts value from the business without adding to it
- The resulting debt service creates an ongoing obligation against future earnings without the productive assets that would have generated those earnings
- The distinguishing test is whether borrowed money funds productive investment (working capital, capex) or distributions (dividends, buyouts, bonuses to owners)
- Productive debt adds capacity the business can later draw on to service the loan; extractive debt adds nothing that helps repay it
- Case: dividend recapitalizations, where a business is loaded with debt to fund a one-time payout to its private equity owners
conversion: Borrowed money that should fund productive investment becomes a debt the business cannot service because the productive capacity to carry it was never built
